intro: We do not publish a rate card, because a plumbing price that is honest depends on what is actually behind the wall. What we can publish is exactly how the charging works, so nothing about your invoice is a surprise. If you take one thing from this page: ask us on the phone whether your job is a free estimate or a service call, and we will tell you the number before anyone is dispatched.

cost_table.heading: What Drives the Number
cost_table.lede: These are the variables we look at when we quote a job in Miami-Dade. None of them are guesses over the phone — they are what the inspection is for.
rows: Remodeling, replacing water or sewer lines, replacing fixtures, new construction — anything more involved than a service call.
Diagnosing and repairing a specific fault. Ask for the service-call figure on the phone; we will give it to you before dispatch.
Time of day, day of week, and whether the water has to be made safe before the repair can start.
Where the blockage sits, whether the line needs a camera, whether jetting is required, and whether a clean-out has to be cut in.
Tank condition, drainfield saturation, depth, access for the excavator, and how much concrete or paving has to come up and go back.
Usually 15–20 minutes. Repairs, if the device fails, are quoted separately — most simple ones we handle in the same visit.
Run length, depth, pipe material, slab or yard, and whether a city sewer connection is part of the work.
cost_table.footnote: Because we own our excavation and concrete-removal equipment and do not sub-contract septic work, the dig and the make-good are inside our quote rather than a second contractor's invoice arriving later.

notes: Estimates are free for work more involved than a service call. We accept credit cards. Licensed C.C. 6469 · Insured CFC057007. Call (305) 446-8141 in Miami or (305) 361-1177 on Key Biscayne.
